newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: Opposition planes bomb Kabul for second day in row.
newsitem.headline: Opposition planes bomb Kabul for second day in row.

text.p: Warplanes belonging to an anti-Taleban alliance bombed the Afghan capital Kabul at dawn on Sunday in the second such raid in 48 hours.

Residents awoke to a deafening barrage of anti-aircraft fire as Taleban gunners opened up on two jets flying high over the city. The planes dropped at least three bombs, but it was not immediately clear where they fell or whether they had caused any casualties or damage.
The raid followed one on Friday night, when an opposition warplane dropped two bombs on Kabul airport. One landed in the air defence section, killing at least one Taleban fighter.
Taleban officials said there was no damage to the runway at the airport, which is used by military and civilian aircraft.
The air strikes followed Taleban bombing raids on Maimana, capital of the northeastern province of Faryab, held by forces loyal to northern opposition leader General Abdul Malik.
A spokesman for Malik, General Humayun Fauzi, said on Friday that Taleban raids had killed 90 people in Maimana within 48 hours, including 40 Taleban prisoners held in the city jail.
Fauzi said two Taleban officials, Foreign Minister Mullah Mohammad Ghous and Civil Aviation Minister Maulvi Akhter Mohammad Mansoor were among 30 wounded in the raids.
But an independent military source said there had been no casualties in the bombing of Maimana.
The Taleban, who captured Kabul in September, are fighting to impose their strict Islamic rule across Afghanistan, but have failed to quell opposition forces in the north.
